title: Building LLM pipelines that do not collapse under production load
excerpt: Prompt engineering gets you to a demo. Architecture gets you to production.
body:
Prompt engineering gets you to a demo. Architecture gets you to production. The gap between the two is wider than most teams expect when they start, and the failure modes are different from those in conventional software systems.

The non-determinism problem

The fundamental challenge of LLM systems in production is that they are probabilistic. The same input will not always produce the same output. Most software architecture assumes deterministic components — test once, trust always. LLM pipelines require a different posture: continuous evaluation, output validation at runtime, and fallback strategies for when the model produces outputs outside acceptable bounds.

Latency is not a linear function of load

Under normal conditions, an LLM API call might take 800ms. Under high load — whether from upstream traffic spikes or provider-side congestion — that same call might take 12 seconds or timeout entirely. Systems that are not designed for this variability tend to cascade: timeouts propagate upstream, queues fill, and what started as a latency problem becomes an availability problem.

The patterns I use: aggressive timeouts with retries on a separate budget, streaming responses where the UX permits, caching at the semantic level for frequently repeated queries, and fallback paths that degrade gracefully to simpler models or cached results rather than returning errors.

Evaluation is infrastructure

The teams that run LLM systems reliably in production treat evaluation as infrastructure — not a phase that happens before launch. They maintain evaluation datasets that grow with observed failures, run automated evaluation pipelines on every model update, and have dashboards that make quality degradation visible before users notice it. Building this is unglamorous. It is also the difference between a system that improves over time and one that quietly gets worse.
